title: A Nanoscale Investigation of Plasma Electrolytic Oxidation Coatings on Mg Alloy: The Role of Electrolyte
content: Surface treatment of Mg alloys by plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO) is one of the major approaches for improving the performance of Mg alloys, otherwise often restricted by hydrogen evolution during corrosion. The thickness, porosity, and morphology of PEO coating are strongly influenced by the process parameters and conditions such as electrolyte, applied voltage/current density, frequency, duty cycle, and treatment time [1]. In a comparative study on the effect of electrolyte concentration in the deposition solution, the macroscopic observation by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) could not support the changes in the corrosion resistance measured, which indicates the possibility of other undocumented factors such as microstructure and chemical composition of the coatings [2]. To better understand the effect of the electrolyte solution, two coated Mg alloys were prepared by plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO) using different alkaline electrolyte solution. We compared the two different coating properties based on results from x-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron-microscopy (SEM), high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (TEM) used to determine the porosity and crystallinity of coating. Finally, atom probe tomography (APT) was employed to quantify the chemical composition and provide a 3D representation of the precipitate location within the coating with nanoscale resolution. Preliminary results show that the coating contains with pores, precipitates and semi amorphous regions (see figure 1). The results help in optimizing the electrolyte and coating for the facilitating the applications of bioresorbable Mg alloys for medical devices [3].
